newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Creditanstalt Q1 profit up,sees good full yr.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Creditanstalt Q1 profit up,sees good full yr.

text.p: Austria's Creditanstalt said on Tuesday first quarter group operating profit hit a record high and offered an even more upbeat outlook for the full year as its chief executive for the past nine years took final leave.
The bank said operating profit in the first three months rose 31 percent to 2.11 billion schillings ($173.2 million), boosted by its strong international business and treasury operations.
For the full year, Creditanstalt said more good news was on the way.
"The very good operating profit of the first months of the current year makes us expect a further gain in full-year net profit compared to 1996," it said in a shareholders' letter.
Last year, Creditanstalt reported a full year net profit of 2.93 billion schillings, up 35 percent from the previous year.
The bank said the first-quarter figures did not include a "net capital gain" of about 1.3 billion schillings from the sale of a 32.8 percent stake in machine maker Maschinenfabrik Andritz last month.

In a statement released ahead of its annual shareholders' meeting, it said first quarter operating earnings rose to 5.31 billion schillings from 4.58 billion a year earlier, while operating expenses increased to 3.20 billion schillings from 2.97 billion a year ago.
Total assets grew 7.3 percent to 737.58 billion at the end of March, it added.
Creditanstalt is controlled by market leader Bank Austria, which in January acquired the state's majority stake in the country's second largest bank for 17.2 billion schillings in cash.

Bank Austria chief executive and Creditanstalt supervisory board head Gerhard Randa told shareholders at the bank's annual general meeting that Erich Hampel was set to be voted as Schmidt-Chiari's successor at a meeting of the supervisory board later on Tuesday.
"The supervisory board has a motion to name Hampel as the new chief executive," Randa said. Bank Austria controls more than 70 percent of Creditanstalt's voting capital.
Hampel, 47, currently chairs the board of postal savings bank PSK, which is due to be split off from the state's postal and telecoms monopoly and partially privatised later this year.

Randa added that Alarich Fenyves, currently in charge of Creditanstalt's international operations, was set to be named as the bank's new vice chief executive, taking over from Max Kothbauer who will leave the bank.
Shareholders also voted to change the official name of the bank to Creditanstalt AG from Creditanstalt-Bankverein AG.

According to the blueprint of the merger deal, which closed the book on Europe's longest running privatisation saga, Bank Austria will keep Creditanstalt as an independent unit for at least five years.
